english: Halt, human.
A hairy beast, towering over you. Its face contorted into a stern (and probably permanent) frown.
Do not pass further.
This is a bugbear.
They are most common in the west, living in the rough lands between Fordnip and the VK.
This woman does not hold power over you.
Do not let her stand in your way.
Yes. This is clearly a female. A real one, capable of terror beyond your sight and sound.
Hello, woman.
I don't like your tone.
How do you do?
Why are you standing down here?
Are you some type of dungeon monster?
She snorts at you.
I don't like your tone, man-thing.
Huh. I was just about to say the same thing. Without the 'man-thing' comment. That's kind of interesting.
(Clear your throat.) "You doing good down here?"
What?
What are you babbling about?
...I'm not sure.
She glares at you.
What were we talking about?
You are not allowed to pass! Back away.
Doing good?
I don't like you.
Now, back off!
She gives you a perplexed look, and gestures in several directions.
I'm working! Go away.
She scoffs. "Yes. Now back off before I smash your face in."
I, Moongore of the Rigid and the HWBT, demands it.
The bugbear places a hand on its weapon.
A morning star. Beware.
A morning star. Is it for you?
Morning star? No, that is clearly just a spiked mace.
I believe the term is 'flanged mace'.
Wait, which one has the ball-on-a-chain, and which one has the ball-on-a-stick?
A CLUB.
Keep it simple.
She will not use it.
She sure keeps her hand on it.
Human.
Watch yourself. This is Halfways territory.
She notices Snell with you, and gives him a nod.
Runner.
Hey, Moongore. Things going well?
They are going.
She nods in your direction. "This is your cleric?"
Seems so, yeah.
I thought he'd be taller, she says with a scoff.
Where is your Runner?
You should not delve into the City Below alone. You will be destroyed.
(Bow.) "I am The Cleric. Nice to meet you."
Snell looks at you like you're crazy.
Huh. I was just about to say the same thing. Except the 'man-thing' comment. That's kind of interesting.
And I don't like you.
I do not believe you, nor your weak frame.
You should get your goblin.
Moongore keeps the Roots safe.
She's our champion of the depths.
She grunts. "No monster will ascend. Not while I draw breath."
...Serious as always. Good to see.
She snorts. "I am Moongore of the Rigid. Servant of Lady Sageleaf."
The bugbear places a hand on her weapon.
Do not cause trouble.
Wait, which one is the ball-on-a-chain, and which one is the ball-on-a-stick?
Keeping it simple. Great.
You. Helmed man-kind.
You're not getting past, helmed man-thing.
No need for that. Since I have no need to pass.
...Are you sure you can't let me pass?
Whom do you serve?
Can I ask you some quick questions?
Can I ask some more... personal questions? (Attempt to flirt.)
E-"Okay. Bye."
Good.
Yes.
She grunts. "I do not recommend it."
There are devilish traps set up along these halls.
And do not enter the crypts. There is an undead guardian.
An undead? But that's the kind of stuff I take care of!
You? No. I do not believe you can take on an undead warrior by yourself.
...You did?
Well. She looks you up and down.
I am impressed. Less for us to worry about.
YES...!
Impressed enough to let me pass?
No.
Darn.
She snorts. "I work for the Halfways. I serve Lady Sageleaf."
So I need to ask her for permission if I want to pass?
I work for the Halfways as well.
She squints, and thinks for a few seconds.
Yes. If she gives you permission, I will let you pass. But I do not think-
She stops mid-sentence.
No you do not. I-
She stops mid-sentence, and squints at you.
Are you a cleric?
I am The Cleric, yes.
More of a wizard, really. But sure.
I like to see myself as a dashing rogue, personally.
Why?
I don't know the difference. I don't care, frankly.
A simpleton. How sad.
A dashing...? No. You are clearly a cleric.
So dismissive.
Hm. A magic music thing?
I'm working on both of those.
Huh.
She scoffs.
Hm.
I heard a cleric was sent. Because of the explosion.
Why are you down here? The Dragon is waiting!
A WHAT?!
(Look around, wildly.) "Where?!"
I'm sorry, I just sort of ended up here.
I don't follow orders. Even if it's from a dragon.
I'm not sure where to go. I'm quite lost.
She groans, loudly.
You fool!
Harsh but true.
I like this bugbear. She understands you well.
I'm talking about Lady Sageleaf! Of the Halfway Bridge Tribe!
What? How?!
You don't simply wander into the City Below!
That is how fools get killed.
Not a dragon. The Dragon.
She will eat you whole if you don't hurry there. Right now.
She shakes her head and sighs.
Head up the stairs. The apple tunnel is usually locked, so you will have to leave the lichhouse by going all the way up.
...Apple tunnel?
(Let her speak.)
Silence!
You head up the stairs, okay?
After that, you head south. Go across the grass. There should be a goblin standing guard.
Listen to her.
Right at the Garden entrance. Talk to him. Are you able to follow these instructions?
Treat her with respect. She's clearly a powerful woman.
Mum.
Yes, ma'am.
Yes, mum.
Possibly.
...Can I hear it again?
The bugbear stops and looks at you with wild rage in her eyes.
Then go!
Her roar causes you to stir.
She reaches forward, grabbing your uniform.
She pulls you in close, yelling in your face, "Up the stairs, across the park, to the Garden!"
She is in control.
Wonderful.
Ew. You have bugbear spit all over your face.
Amazing.
Then she lets you go, before taking a step back.
Go. Now.
No!
She is, indeed, disgusted with you.
Not necessarily a problem.
I will not entertain you with an answer.
Now leave.
I have some questions about the day of the tea shop explosion.
What's it like working for the HWBT?
You look like a great warrior... and woman. (Attempt to flirt.)
E-(Nod your head and leave.)
I have realized that.
She looks mad.
Understandable.
You're not gonna punch me or something? Maybe bite?
It's a nice shield.
I will get it back.
For now, my allegiance to Lady Sageleaf forbids me from <shake>crushing your bones</shake>.
I recommend not trying your luck any further.
Oh, lord Urth. This is life.
This is what it's all about.
You got lucky! Neat.
...A TROLL?
The hairy woman gives you a wicked smile.
I'd say you were lying, but I don't think you're up for that.
This will surely help.
He did actually kill a troll. Technically speaking. It was just-
Silence, she interrupts him.
She nods in your direction.
Well done, human. I find your skills highly arousing.
Thank you, I made them myself.
(Stay quiet and just smirk like a madman within your helm.)
(Stay quiet and just smirk like a madman within your bucket.)
(Stay quiet and just smirk like a madman within your pot.)
The bugbear scoffs and clenches her morning star.
Now what else do you with to speak of? I will not indulge your ego any more than this, I assure you.
She will not meet your gaze. How strange.
OH man. Yep. Halfway there, boy.
Glory be, as glory found- the greatest man will not be bound- to foreign lands and foreign shores, the loving heart will open doors.
Oh... oh...
Ohhh... ohhhh...
This is a shame.
This is all such a shame.
A roper?
That is a ferocious beast. They do not come this far up very often.
Well done, human.
Keep killing things, and being MANLY. She likes it.
Moongore doesn't turn around, and just grunts at you.
That's Nessan. She's our druid.
She's not very responsive.
Do not disturb her. Not that you would be able to.
She is deep in meditation. Far from here.
Leave her alone.
But I need to talk to her!
Fine. I'll do that.
Then find her in the Garden later.
She spends her mornings down here, and returns to her office after lunch.
I have cooked her a lovely mushroom stew today.
I have cooked her a lovely roasted cave crab today.
I have cooked her a lovely herb-crusted fish today.
I have cooked her a lovely root vegetable medley today.
I have cooked her a lovely spiced meat pie today.
I have cooked her a lovely underground greens salad today.
I have cooked her a lovely braised tunnel rabbit today.
You cook?
You eat lunch together?
Yes. It is a part of my duties.
Can I join?
Sounds lovely.
You may NOT.
A terrible tragedy.
To be forced to avoid suffering food poisoning.
I'm great at cooking. So yes, it is.
I felt a slight rumble in the earth.
I was down here, guarding the Roots.
So nothing too out of the ordinary?
Just a little rumble?
Alright. I've got some other questions.
Nothing I have to tell you, human.
I'm assuming it was a most ferocious force of magic or nature, if it created a quake all the way down here.
Fine.
She grunts.
Funny noise.
This beast can't even speak properly.
Is that a yes?
(Grunt back.)
Speak clearly, bugbear.
She bares her fangs.
I did.
Are you looking for this man?
Yeah well, clearly.
(Grunt, conspicuously.)
The bugbear shows you a deep frown and says, "If you see him, stick a knife through his heart for me."
Speak her tongue.
Wait, why?
(Grunt, questioningly.)
I saw him approaching from the Pillar chamber. Told him to stop, to step away from Halfway turf.
But that bastard...
He cast a spell on me.
That handsome, huh?
That's awful.
If you failed to resist it, that's on you.
(Grunt, empathetically.)
What? No.
He was as ugly as the rest of you.
Ouch.
You think I'm ugly?
Yes. Humans really suck, don't they?
I cannot see your face, human.
But I would assume so, yes.
I did not say that.
You harmless flaccid cock.
No. I was weak.
She scoffs. "Yes, I agree."
Are you mocking me, human?
No. The exact opposite.
Yes. But not in a bad way.
Possibly. I'm not sure.
Yeah.
Do not mock me in a good way, either.
She shakes her head.
I saw him approaching. He wore an ugly yellow robe.
Then he said a few words, and I suddenly happily allowed him to pass.
A charm of some kind. I was helpless, like a kitten.
Gods, I hate kittens.
You can fix her.
Run away from her. Before it's too late.
You... hate kittens?
What else can you tell me about him?
M-"In which direction did he go?"
Yes. Any child-beast, really.
They are too weak to survive on their own. That is a disgusting feature of adolescence.
This chick is crazy-crazy.
You can fix her.
Okay?
You must find this man and punish him.
That way you can earn her respect.
Do what you want. I do not care.
She actually kind of does.
You catch her glancing at your figure.
He had slightly darker skin. Unlike most pale humans in Norvik.
He carried a backpack. And several... things. Tools.
That's not very specific.
How much darker, exactly?
You want wordy? Go ask a poet.
Somewhere between a tan hill goblin and pale fell orcs.
That's very good information, thank you.
I have no idea what that means.
She shrugs.
Through the South Caves.
She points towards the damp tunnel down the slope.
I warned him about the monsters as he walked away. Because of that darned spell.
I would have hoped for him to be dinner for some Hook Horror or Darkmantle... but the bastard turned invisible as he entered the tunnel.
I hate wizards.
I'm a wizard, by the way.
Same. Can't stand those nerds.
I'm neutral on them personally.
(Grunt, angrily.)
Then I hate you.
The bugbear lets out a grunt.
Clearly signaling she's done with this part of the conversation.
You did?
The bugbear lifts her chin and looks down on you.
Is he in the City Below still?!
No. He is far below.
No. I found him captured by a troll.
Oh. That is good! He deserves pain.
Well. Speaking of which...
Mm?
I punched him in the face.
You did?!
She clears her throat, but it sounds more like a surprised growl.
...You did?
I did. I avenged your honor.
Hm...
This imposing fluffy monster looks you up and down with a smirk.
I must have misjudged you, human.
Maybe you are a real man after all.
YEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEES.
Careful now. Real smooth...
Invite her to fight thugs in Housing. That should work.
Meek is happy for master! Meek did not know human need prove humanness. Very good hairy woman trust master now!
As a real man, perhaps you'd like to go on a date sometime, then?
Perhaps you'd like to... go out sometime. Dinner?
Come with me. We can go fight thugs in Housing, or something.
Thanks. Anyway... (Don't ask her out.)
Oh! Meek sorry!
Hope master score! Very hard!
She gives you a nod.
NOOOOOOOOOOOOO!
But...
She gives you a nod and a grin.
A sparring match. In the Garden.
After the election, of course. I'm on duty until then.
A physical meeting with this handsome woman?
This is a massive win for you and your manhood.
I'll take it!
R-"No. I've earned something more."
Good. We will set a time later.
She scoffs. "Something more?!"
A deep frown appears on her face.
You dare throw my offer away, human?
Demand more.
Nevermind, I'll take it...!
You feel your muscles quake.
The earth itself is MOVED by your LOINS.
Oh gods.
Simply speak your mind. You know she will hear you.
I battled a TROLL for you. Show me some appreciation.
Her frown fades, replaced by a wicked smile.
Then she grabs your uniform, pulling you closer.
Much, much closer.
She opens her maw. Right over the little piece of space left between your neck and your chainmail.
And then she...
Bites down.
ATTACHED.
Hard. Hard enough to leave a solid mark.
A violent union.
Then she lets go, both with her maw and her claws.
Appreciation. Hope you enjoy.
This is what you get when you chase crazy.
This  is  a  real  woman.
<wiggle>Yesthankyouthatwasverynicethanks</wiggle>.
(Mutter incoherently.)
You can let me know when you have time later. For our sparring match.
Your body gives out.
It does not listen to you.
But... I HAVE to...!
It would come at a great toll.
If you are certain you wish to pay it. Then... do so.
I PAY THE BUGBEAR TOLL. (Inflict great pain on yourself.)
Uh. Nevermind, I'll just take the original offer.
Everything hurts as you push yourself forward.
Then...
She laughs. "That's better."
I will set a time for us later.
Now... is there anything else you need, you puny human male?
No, of course not.
I got this as a gift. I can't just give it away.
Oh.
Okay, then.
There is great respect for the elven druid.
Just take it, then. Leave the convo, sneak up on her, and snatch it.
Only suckers ask for things.
That would be stealing.
Yes. It would.
It would be wrong.
Oh yes. So wrong. SO bad.
Let's do it.
Okay.
Okay.
The dark dwarf. Yes. He asked for access to the south tunnels.
He is not permitted.
Why not?
Because he's a dwarf? A dark dwarf?
The Lady does not permit it.
No. He is not permitted because he is a dungeoneer.
Lady Sageleaf does not allow looters on her grounds.
Only official expeditions.
Am I an official expedition?
Good. He seems like a profiteer. I hate those.
Seems a bit discriminatory.
She glances at Snell, who shrugs.
More or less.
I have no strong feeling on that.
But Lady Sageleaf does not will it.
It is not.
She frowns.
If you go into the south tunnels, beware of monsters. They crawl in from below, infesting the caverns.
We clean them out every other week, but they return often.
Isn't the Pest Control Guild supposed to take care of that stuff?
What kind of monsters?
She lets out a deep laugh.
Pest Control?!
Those pussies won't step below the Lower. Especially on Tolstad.
Bunch of weaklings looking for easy payouts. If we can't deal with it ourselves, we hire outside muscle. But not the PCG.
Historically, the PCG have trouble dealing with the massive amount of requests of monsters and esoterical things crawling through Norvik.
You've heard many tales of the Pest Controllers in your days.
The Pest Control Guild works closely with clerics. Whenever they need heavy muscle.
Back in the day, retired Clerics would often gravitate towards the PCG. But these days, most clerics don't want to get their hands dirty in that sort of way.
Dangerous work. Stay away from it.
Dangerous work. For real men.
All kinds. Anything that crawls through the cracks of the City Below.
All kinds? Tell me more.
Don't tell me. I want it to be a surprise.
She gives you a stern, but slightly concerned look.
You are insane, man-thing.
I like that.
Last month we killed a Hook Horror. It was a great hunt.
Before that a bunch of Giant Spiders. A Gray Ooze. Last year we had to get a specialist to deal with a hive of Cranium Ants.
They negotiated for days.
The worst was probably the Gricks. I hate those things. But I'm sad to say we have not yet had to deal with a Bulette.
I do not think those land sharks enjoy tunneling here. But there have been reports of a few of them moving closer to settlements in the last year, over in Verdune.
I want to skin one of those things, one day. That would be pleasurable.
(Stare at her.)
...Cool.
She grins.
I can deal with that. I'm very strong.
She looks you up and down.
Mm.
They are good.
Lady Sageleaf is a great leader.
Her power is overwhelming.
You look a lot stronger than her, though.
I agree. That little goblin woman is enough to break a dozen men.
She's not that scary.
R-"Lady Sageleaf is a weak, inefficient leader who will fall soon enough."
I am not.
Do not even imply that, human.
Or more.
I suggest you lose that foolish thought, human. If you wish to keep your head.
The goblin contains a laugh, before giving you a shocked glance.
It's your funeral, he mutters and takes a step back.
Take that back, she says with a stern face.
Right away. Take those filthy words back.
I... I take it back?
You might be a fool, but you can at least learn. Like a dog.
Take. It. Back.
...Okay. Sorry.
NO! I don't want to!
That's better.
She gets closer. "I will have your tongue if you do not."
Fine. I take it back.
She holds up a fist. "This close."
The bugbear slaps you across your helm, sending it spinning, along with your mind.
Take it back!
Take it back! Now!
She takes a step back with a foul grin. "Good."
Holy hells...
The bugbear holds up her hand to slap you again, her chest heaving from heavy breaths.
While clearly having a great endurance, this woman is exhausted from slapping you so many times.
You. Stand. Tall.
W-what?
Hit me again, woman.
She glares at you, with wide eyes.
Fear.
Envy.
Respect.
She lowers her hand. "I will let it slide. This time."
She gives you a slow nod.
You feel POWERFUL.
(Clear your throat.) "Anyway, back to my question. What's it like working for the HWBT?"
She looks away for a moment.
I've been given a life here. A purpose.
While I do not enjoy living among your kind, the goblins are a fine people.
Thanks.
Not you in particular. Weasel.
Weasel?! I don't think I deserve to be called that.
